title: Stick to the Gym
meta_desc: Discover research-backed tips to help you stick to your gym routine in New Zealand, including habit formation, accountability, and tracking your progress.
intro: Getting into a gym routine can be tough, but sticking to it can be even harder. New Zealand research shows that forming good habits and having a support system are key to long-term success. In this guide, we'll explore practical tips to help you make the most of your gym membership and achieve your fitness goals. With the help of Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme, you can get 40-70% off your gym membership, making it easier to get started.

sections.heading: Habit Formation
sections.body: The first step to sticking to your gym routine is to form a habit. This means creating a schedule and sticking to it, even on weekends and days off. Research shows that it takes around 66 days to form a new habit, so be patient and don't get discouraged if you miss a day or two. Many NZ gyms, such as City Fitness and Les Mills, offer flexible membership options that allow you to attend classes or use the gym at times that suit you.
list: Start small: begin with 2-3 times per week and gradually increase frequency
Schedule it in: treat your gym sessions as non-negotiable appointments
Track your progress: use a fitness tracker or log your workouts to monitor progress

sections.heading: Accountability and Support
sections.body: Having a support system is crucial to sticking to your gym routine. This can be a friend, family member, or personal trainer who can motivate and encourage you to reach your goals. Many NZ gyms, such as Jetts and Anytime Fitness, offer personal training sessions or small group training classes that can provide an added level of accountability and support.
list: Find a gym buddy: having someone to hold you accountable can make a big difference
Join a fitness class: group classes can be a great way to meet new people and stay motivated
Hire a personal trainer: one-on-one training can provide tailored guidance and support

sections.heading: Morning vs Evening Workouts
sections.body: The age-old debate: when is the best time to work out? The answer depends on your personal preferences and schedule. Some people prefer morning workouts to get their day started, while others prefer evening workouts to unwind after a long day. Research shows that there is no significant difference in terms of weight loss or fitness gains, so it ultimately comes down to what works best for you. Many NZ gyms, such as Les Mills and City Fitness, offer 24/7 access, making it easy to fit in a workout at a time that suits you.
list: Experiment with different times: find what works best for your schedule and energy levels
Consider your goals: if you're trying to lose weight, morning workouts may be more effective
Listen to your body: if you're not a morning person, don't force it - work out in the evening instead

sections.heading: Gym Buddy Culture in NZ
sections.body: New Zealand has a thriving gym culture, with many gyms offering a supportive and social environment. Joining a gym with a strong community can make a big difference to your motivation and enjoyment. Look for gyms that offer social events, group classes, and personal training sessions to help you connect with like-minded people. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can also help you find a gym that suits your needs and budget.
list: Research local gyms: look for gyms with a strong community and social events
Attend group classes: a great way to meet new people and stay motivated
Join online forums: connect with other gym-goers and stay up-to-date with the latest fitness trends

sections.heading: Get Started
sections.body: Now that you've learned some research-backed tips to help you stick to your gym routine, it's time to get started. Remember to start small, be patient, and don't be afraid to ask for help. With the right mindset and support, you can achieve your fitness goals and enjoy the many benefits of regular exercise.
